title: one file-lock helper in tools/base stands for fcntl.flock, so the inference host, the metrics collector and their proofs import on Windows
intention: a single helper cairn/tools/base/flock.py takes and releases an advisory file lock the same way on POSIX (fcntl.flock) and Windows (msvcrt.locking on one byte), and host.py and metrics.py take their locks through it, so both import and lock on Windows and are unchanged on POSIX.
why: Measured 2026-11-12 on akiendell: 13 proofs raise ModuleNotFoundError: No module named fcntl, eleven of them through inference_domain/host.py:64 and the rest through cairn/metrics.py:12
traces_to: Law 4: the import scan is the physics that keeps a bare import fcntl out of the two modules; Law 3: the failure was measured as ModuleNotFoundError at the import line in thirteen proofs.
how: Add cairn/tools/base/flock.py with lock(fd_or_file, exclusive=True, block=True) and unlock(fd_or_file). On POSIX it is fcntl.flock with LOCK_EX or LOCK_SH, plus LOCK_NB when block is false; on nt it is msvcrt.locking on byte 0 (LK_LOCK/LK_NBLCK). A contended non-blocking take raises BlockingIOError on both. fcntl and msvcrt are imported inside the branch for the host OS, never at module top for the other. host.py and metrics.py replace their fcntl.flock calls and drop import fcntl. Red-first proof cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_flock_stands_for_fcntl.py: (1) with sys.modules['fcntl'] set to None in a subprocess, host.py and metrics.py import, which reds on Linux against the unedited modules; (2) an ast scan finds no top-level import fcntl in those two files; (3) two descriptors on one file: the second non-blocking exclusive take raises BlockingIOError, and succeeds after unlock. The four modules that already carry an inline branch are not touched.

clauses.claim: importing cairn.devices.inference_domain.host and cairn.devices.cairn.metrics succeeds in a subprocess where sys.modules['fcntl'] is None, where the unedited modules raise ModuleNotFoundError
a non-blocking exclusive take on a file another descriptor holds raises BlockingIOError, and the same take succeeds once the holder unlocks
neither host.py nor metrics.py has a module-level import fcntl
